(This evening through next Sunday)

WEATHER PATTERN OVERVIEW: Satellite loop is showing mostly cloudy
skies over all of northern and central Nevada at this time. Winds
are generally breezy with gusts to 25 mph in the north, but much
stronger winds are being felt in central Nevada with gusts of 35
to 40 mph seen in Ely, Eureka, and Tonopah. Look for the winds to
remain somewhat elevated during the overnight hours. Lows tonight
will be in the 20s and 30s.

The main weather maker is an upper level trough with an axis that
is currently moving onshore in California. The upper level trough
will continue moving through the west with impacts through
tomorrow across the area. Light rain showers are being shown on
radar in Humboldt county at this time and these showers will keep
moving to the east during evening hours. Models continue to show a
fairly vigorous cold front that will be pushing into western and
west-central Nevada later this evening and tonight. A cross-
section of the US Highway 50 corridor is showing signs of strong
lift combining with instability and moisture through the dendritic
growth zone during the early portions of tomorrow morning. Current
snow totals have been adjusted upward but there is concern of 
narrow banded moderate to heavy snow occurring across a line 
including Austin-Eureka-Ely-Great Basin National Park. Snow totals
are coming in at around one to four inches in these locations, 
but locally higher amounts of three to seven inches may be 
possible across the higher passes and summits as well as in the 
aforementioned locations should a narrow band set up over them. 
Another concern with the frontal passage is brief snow squall 
conditions. Expecting a fairly quick changeover from rain, to rain
and snow mix, to all snow, and combining with brief strong winds 
as the direction changes to the west and northwest so visibility 
values could drop quickly to one-half mile or less in the heaviest
snow showers. Finally, there is some weak CAPE that could help to
promote isolated rumbles of thunder during the morning hours 
Tuesday in central Nevada. Further north, amounts along the I-80 
corridor continue to be up to a half inch or so, with higher 
amounts of one to three inches over the summits and passes on 
I-80. Further north in northern Elko county snow amounts of one to
four inches are forecast with the highest amounts likely in the 
Jarbidge wilderness. The snow showers will change to a rain and 
snow mix during the mid-morning hours as high temperatures try to 
rebound into the upper 30s to low 40s. By the end of the 
afternoon, any showers will diminish from west to east with 
partial clearing by late afternoon and evening as a weak shortwave
ridge builds in. Overnight lows will be in the teens to low 20s.

The quiet weather will not last long as the ridge quickly
exits out of the area Wednesday morning with the next storm 
system on its heels late morning Wednesday. Scattered rain showers
will develop in Humboldt county, moving east during the day and 
night. This system will bring in much colder air versus the last 
system and so expecting snow showers to develop during the 
overnight. Afternoon highs will mainly be in the 30s, with a few 
sites trying hard to make it into the low 40s. Winds will be 
breezy during the afternoon in central Nevada with gusts to 30 to 
35 mph in the afternoon. Snow levels will continue on a quick 
downward trend and will be at the valley floors. Overnight lows 
will be in the 20s.

The upper level trough will continue moving towards and over
northern and central Nevada Thursday and Thursday night. Storm
total snow amounts are expected to be highest across central
Nevada with about two to five inches possible, with up to one or two
inches in northern Nevada through Friday. Winter weather headlines
may be needed for parts of central Nevada for this system. High
temperatures Thursday and Friday will be well below normal with
readings in the 30s to maybe the low 40s. Lows will be in the
teens, though Saturday morning could see the single digits to
teens, depending on the amount of snow on the ground, clearing
skies, and drier air working into the area due to shortwave
ridging.

The potential exists for yet another system coming in for the end
of the forecast period, though confidence remains very low at this
time. Temperatures will remain on the cold side with highs in the
30s and 40s with lows in the teens.

FORECAST CONFIDENCE & DEVIATIONS: Edits were made to the winds,
PoPs, weather, and slight additions to the snow amounts from the
NBM forecast through the short term. Confidence is high in the 
next system affecting the forecast area through roughly Tuesday. 
Confidence in qpf and snow totals is low at this time due to the 
potential for locally higher amounts, especially across southern 
Lander/Eureka, White Pine, and northwest and northeast Nye 
counties. Confidence is moderate in the Wednesday through Friday 
system bringing additional snowfall
